FISHY FEAST - a RetroStone VC game for Windows
(c) 2026 Pierre-Louis Boyer (8BCraft). Code MIT, art/music/sound CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: see LICENSE-fishyfeast.txt.

You are a little fish in a big pond. Nibble the plankton to grow, swallow
any fish clearly smaller than you, and keep away from the bigger ones: the
bigger you grow, the slower you swim and the more of the pond you see.
Fifteen bot fish share the pond: greedy grazers, timid ones, hunters and
opportunists. Split (A) to snap up a fish that thinks it is safe (press
again: 4, 8, 16 pieces; each piece can be eaten on its own, and they merge
back after a while), spit a pellet (B) to bait one, lure a big bully onto a
sea urchin and watch it burst, hide under the spikes when you are small.
Big fish slowly shrink. One life: your score is the biggest you ever grew.
Medals at 80, 250, 600 and 1200, and your best is kept.

Run FishyFeast.exe. No installation needed (SDL2 is built in).

Controls                  Gamepad (SNES layout)      Keyboard
  swim (8 directions)       D-pad                      arrow keys
  split                     A                          X
  eject a pellet            B (hold: more)             Z
  start                     A (or B, Start, D-pad)     X or Enter
  pause / resume            Select (or Start in a run) Backspace or Esc
  players 2-4 join          A on their pad, on the title (B leaves)
  back to the title         A (or Select) on the results
  touch / mouse             a finger down on the left part and dragged: a
                            stick (swim that way); the round SPLIT and EJECT
                            buttons at the bottom right; a tap starts

Up to four fish (orange, blue, green and purple) swim together in split
screen, each with their own pad; players can eat each other. Each is out when
eaten, the game ends when all are out, and the results rank everyone by the
biggest mass they reached, with medals.

F11 or Alt+Enter: fullscreen. F12: screenshot. Close the window to quit.
Options: FishyFeast.exe --scale 4 --fullscreen
The best score is saved in fishyfeast.srm next to the exe.
